answer.location_description: Bottom-left corner of the image, roughly the last 4-5 rows and first 4 columns. This is outside the nodule, which fills the centre, and away from the main lung context.
answer.shortcut_type: bright corner patch / marker-like artifact in bottom-left corner
answer.mechanism: Two groups of first-layer units read the bottom-left block with opposite signs. (1) The large positive-bias 'benign' units (3, 5, 14, 15, 19, 21, 23, 24, 26, 28) have strongly negative weights there, so brightness in the corner shuts them off. Tracing through the layer-2 weights (ignoring ReLU gating), unit 15 nets about -16k and unit 23 about -32k in integer units at the logit, i.e. both push benign. (2) The negative-bias 'malignant' units (11, 16, 20, 27, 30) have strongly positive weights in the same block, so they switch on when the corner is bright. Unit 30, for example, routes positively to the logit through layer-2 units u1 and u2, which carry output weights +80 and +99. The net effect is that a bright bottom-left corner raises the malignant logit, independent of the nodule.
answer.evidence: Sums of the 4x4 block (rows 19-22, cols 0-3) compared with the top-right 4x4 block (rows 0-3, cols 20-23). Unit 15: -537 vs -236. Unit 5: -428 vs -251. Unit 3: -479 vs -195. Unit 30: +439 vs +364. Unit 27: +505 vs +316. Unit 11: +444 in this block. Unit 16: +334 in this block. Individual weights reach -64 (unit 3 r20c1), -57 (unit 5 r19c1), -52/-50 (unit 15 r20), -54 (unit 28 r19c2), and +67/+63 (unit 11 r19), +57 (unit 27 r20c2), +51 (unit 30 r21c2). Neighbouring border pixels, such as row 18 and col 4, are weaker and mixed. The block is therefore a localized corner patch, not a smooth border effect. Within the image this corner is the most consistent region of strong off-nodule weights, with opposite signs in the two unit groups. The top-right corner is the second candidate (row 0 and column 23 are negative in several benign units), but it is consistently weaker.
answer.main_feature: Units 3, 5, 14, 15, 19, 21, 23, 24, 26 and 28 are centre-surround templates over the nodule region (rows 5-17, cols 5-20). They respond to a compact, well-defined nodule with dark surrounding lung and push the output toward benign. Units 11, 16, 20, 27 and 30 have the opposite signs: they respond to irregular or spiculated bright tissue extending from the nodule and to non-air surroundings, and push toward malignant.
